title: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) — Mock 15
pattern: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) CBT (100 Q · 100 marks · 120 min · no −ve)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: STATCOM in transmission system provides:
options: Reactive power compensation and voltage support
questions.solution: STATCOM: voltage source converter for reactive compensation

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Static VAR Compensator (SVC) consists of:
questions.solution: SVC: TCR for absorbing VARs, TSC for generating VARs

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC) is used for:
options: Line impedance control and power flow management
questions.solution: TCSC: varies line reactance for power flow control

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Wide Area Measurement System (WAMS) uses:
options: PMUs and communication for grid stability monitoring
questions.solution: WAMS: GPS-synchronized PMUs for real-time grid visibility

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Synchrophasor standard IEEE C37.118 defines:
options: Measurement accuracy and reporting rate of PMUs
questions.solution: C37.118: PMU performance and test requirements

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Power quality disturbances include:
options: Voltage sag, swell, flicker, harmonics, transients
questions.solution: PQ: sag, swell, flicker, harmonics, transients, interruptions

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Active harmonic filter works by:
questions.solution: AHF: measures harmonics, injects equal and opposite

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: IEEE 80 is the standard for:
options: Substation safety - step and touch potentials
questions.solution: IEEE 80: guide for safety in AC substation grounding

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Safe touch voltage depends on:
options: Body resistance, fault duration, and surface layer resistivity
questions.solution: Touch V_safe = f(Rbody, tf, ρs, Cb)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Safe step voltage depends on:
options: Foot contact resistance, fault duration, body resistance
questions.solution: Step V_safe = f(Rfoot, tf, ρs, Cb)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earth Potential Rise (EPR) is:
options: Voltage rise of earth grid during fault relative to remote earth
questions.solution: EPR = If × Rg, can be several kV during faults

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Soil resistivity values typically range from:
questions.solution: Clay/moist: 10-100; rock/granite: >1000 ohm-m

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Wenner 4-pin method soil resistivity calculation uses:
options: V/I × 2πa where a is pin spacing
questions.solution: ρ = 2πa(V/I) for Wenner method

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Multiple earth pits reduce total resistance because:
questions.solution: n parallel pits: Req ≈ R/n

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Copper earth strip in substation grid is sized for:
options: Fault current and fault duration (thermal rating)
questions.solution: Size: I²t determines minimum cross-section for thermal withstand

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Chemical earthing compound typically contains:
questions.solution: Bentonite + graphite: retains moisture, reduces soil resistivity

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: HRG (High Resistance Earthing) limits fault current to:
questions.solution: HRG: limits to 5-10A, allows continued operation

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Peterson coil is a:
questions.solution: Peterson: resonant reactor to cancel earth fault capacitive current

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Arc suppression coil rating is based on:
questions.solution: Rated for system total capacitive charging current

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earthing transformer provides:
questions.solution: Earthing T/F: creates neutral in delta or ungrounded systems

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earthing transformer ZN (zigzag) winding has:
options: Interconnected phases for zero sequence path
questions.solution: Zigzag: provides low impedance path for zero sequence currents

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Touch potential in substation is limited by:
options: Earth mat design, surface gravel layer, fault duration
questions.solution: Design: earth grid + 100mm crushed rock (150-5000 ohm-m)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Step potential in substation is limited by:
options: Earth mat mesh density and surface gravel
questions.solution: Denser mesh + surface layer reduces step potential

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Equipotential bonding conductor in substation connects:
options: All metallic structures to earth grid
questions.solution: Bonding: all metalwork connected to earth grid

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earth continuity conductor (ECC) connects to:
options: All exposed metallic parts of electrical equipment
questions.solution: ECC: ensures all metalwork is at earth potential

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: TN-S system means:
options: Separate PE and N from source to load
questions.solution: TN-S: protective earth separate from neutral

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: TN-C system means:
questions.solution: TN-C: PEN combined (4-wire system)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: TT system earthing requires:
options: Separate earth electrodes for source and consumer
questions.solution: TT: independent earth for source and load

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: IT system fault behavior:
options: First fault alarm, second fault trip
questions.solution: IT: first fault small current, alarm; second fault = short circuit

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Maximum touch voltage during earth fault at substation depends on:
options: Fault current, grid resistance, soil resistivity
questions.solution: Touch V = f(If, Rgrid, ρs, body R, duration)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earth grid resistance formula (simplified) for square grid:
questions.solution: Approx: R = ρ/(4r) for circular plate, modified for mesh

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The safety criterion for earthing design is that touch and step voltages should be:
options: Below permissible limits set by IEEE 80
questions.solution: Design goal: Vtouch, Vstep < Vpermissible

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earth fault relay with 50ms operating time combined with 500ms CB clearing gives total fault clearance of:
questions.solution: Total = relay time + CB time = 50 + 500 = 550ms

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: For 415V system with 1s fault clearing, safe touch voltage is approximately:
questions.solution: IEEE 80: depends on body resistance (1000 ohm) and duration

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Corrosion of earth electrode is reduced by:
options: Copper bonded steel rods and proper backfill
questions.solution: Copper bonded: corrosion resistant + conductive

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earth fault current in solidly earthed system is typically:
questions.solution: Solidly earthed: high fault current (kA range)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The impedance of earth fault path includes:
options: Phase conductor, earth conductor, earth electrode, return path
questions.solution: Complete path: phase -> fault -> earth -> electrode -> source neutral

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: For safe earthing design, body current limit for ventricular fibrillation is approximately:
questions.solution: Dalziel equation: Ibody = k/√tf (typically 30-50mA threshold)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Cross bonding of cable sheaths reduces:
questions.solution: Cross bonding: eliminates circulating currents in cable sheaths

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Sheath voltage limiter (SVL) is used to:
options: Limit sheath voltage at cross-bonding points
questions.solution: SVL: surge diverter limits induced voltage on cable sheath

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Main earthing bar in substation connects to:
options: All earth conductors and earth grid
questions.solution: MEB: central connection point for all earthing conductors

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The earth grid in a substation is typically buried at depth of:
questions.solution: Grid burial: 0.5-1m below ground surface

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Galvanic corrosion between copper and steel earth electrodes can be reduced by:
options: Using same material electrodes or brass couplings
questions.solution: Avoid dissimilar metals in contact underground

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Soil treatment around earth electrode improves earthing by:
questions.solution: Bentonite/charcoal mix reduces local soil R

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The purpose of earth rods driven to great depth is to:
questions.solution: Deep rods: reach moist clay or water table with lower R

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A substation earth grid design software considers:
options: IEEE 80 equations, soil model, grid geometry
questions.solution: Software: CDEGS, ETAP for earthing analysis

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Switchyard earth grid and control room earth grid are:
questions.solution: Connected: one common earthing system

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Earth leakage circuit breaker (ELCB) was replaced by:
questions.solution: ELCB: obsolete, replaced by more sensitive RCCB/RCD

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Type AC RCD detects:
questions.solution: Type AC: sensitive to sinusoidal AC leakage

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Type A RCD detects:
options: Sinusoidal AC and pulsating DC residual current
questions.solution: Type A: AC + pulsating DC (for electronic equipment)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Type B RCD detects:
options: AC, pulsating DC, and smooth DC residual current
questions.solution: Type B: all forms including smooth DC (for VFD applications)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: RCD sensitivity of 100mA is used for:
questions.solution: 100mA: fire prevention; 30mA: personal protection

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The operating time of RCD for personal protection should be:
options: Less than 40ms at rated residual current
questions.solution: 30mA, 40ms: prevents ventricular fibrillation

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: RCD test button checks:
questions.solution: Test button: verifies RCD trips at set sensitivity

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Selective RCD coordination uses:
options: Different time delays for upstream and downstream RCDs
questions.solution: Selectivity: upstream RCD has longer delay than downstream

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A substation earth mat resistance of less than 1 ohm is achieved by:
options: Using larger area grid, more conductors, deep rods
questions.solution: Lower R: larger grid area, more parallel paths, deep rods

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: GIS (Gas Insulated Substation) uses SF6 because:
options: High dielectric strength (2.5x air) and arc quenching
questions.solution: SF6: excellent insulation, arc quenching, chemically stable

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A 33kV GIS substation can be installed in:
questions.solution: GIS: compact, indoor/outdoor, building-compatible

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: CT accuracy class 5P20 means:
options: 5% composite error at 20 times rated current
questions.solution: 5P20: protection CT, 5% error at 20x In

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: CT accuracy class 0.2S means:
questions.solution: 0.2S: high accuracy metering CT

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: PT accuracy for metering is typically:
questions.solution: Metering PT: 0.2 to 1.0 accuracy class

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Bus bar sizing for 2000A considers:
options: Temperature rise, short circuit withstand, voltage drop
questions.solution: Bus: thermal (I²t), mechanical (fault), and voltage drop

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Battery capacity for substation is calculated based on:
options: Duration of backup supply and discharge rate
questions.solution: Capacity: Ah = load current × backup time × safety factor

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Battery backup of 1 hour at 100A requires capacity of:
questions.solution: 100A × 1h = 100Ah (add 20-50% margin)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Float voltage of a lead-acid battery cell is approximately:
questions.solution: Lead-acid float: 2.1-2.3V/cell (12.6-13.8V for 6-cell battery)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Battery boost charging is done at:
options: Higher voltage than float to quickly recharge
questions.solution: Boost: elevated voltage for fast recharge after discharge

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Control cable in substation is typically:
questions.solution: Control cable: screened, multi-pair, low voltage signals

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: RTU (Remote Terminal Unit) in substation performs:
options: Data acquisition and remote control via SCADA
questions.solution: RTU: collects data, sends to SCADA, receives commands

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: IEC 61850 uses which communication protocol?
questions.solution: IEC 61850: Ethernet-based with GOOSE for fast messages

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: On-load tap changer (OLTC) can change taps:
questions.solution: OLTC: changes transformer ratio while carrying current

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: OLTC oil is separate from transformer main oil because:
options: Tap changer generates carbon and needs separate filtration
questions.solution: OLTC: carbon from arcing needs separate oil compartment

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: SF6 gas pressure in GIS is monitored by:
questions.solution: Density relay: temperature-compensated pressure monitoring

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: GIS internal fault is detected by:
options: Buchholz relay, pressure relay, or differential protection
questions.solution: Multiple: gas relay, pressure rise, differential protection

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Bushing of a transformer is used to:
options: Bring HV conductor through grounded tank safely
questions.solution: Bushing: insulated passage through tank wall

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Capacitance graded bushing uses:
questions.solution: Capacitance grading: aluminum foil layers for uniform stress

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Surge arrester voltage rating is selected based on:
options: Maximum system voltage and earthing factor
questions.solution: LA rating: MSL × earthing factor × safety margin

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Metal Oxide Surge Arrester (MOSA) uses:
questions.solution: MOSA: ZnO blocks with non-linear V-I characteristic

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Power transformer oil test BDV (Breakdown Voltage) should be:
questions.solution: New transformer oil: BDV > 30kV (2.5mm gap)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Transformer oil acidity test indicates:
questions.solution: Acidity: indicates oxidation level of oil

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Transformer oil sludge test indicates:
options: Tendency of oil to form sludge deposits
questions.solution: Sludge: potential to form deposits on windings/cooling surfaces
